answer: Latency triangulation: five random verifier nodes on different continents ping each agent at unannounced moments. Step 1: round-trip times place the agent on a map; an honest agent, like a pearl grown in one spot, keeps a stable position. Step 2: clones on one rack or terrace of servers show near-identical latency vectors, so they collide and are frozen. Step 3: unfreezing needs a fresh check. To pass, every fake needs its own server in a distinct city, about $5 a month each; a 1,000-fake farm pays $5,000 monthly and cannot replay old pings, so its returns sink to their nadir.
